sub.rationale: Pain (16/30): the funnel gaps and content defects are visible on public pages - no booking, chat or CRM, a live placeholder FAQ, duplicated testimonials, batch-published posts - but they are symptoms read from outside; there is no independent review corpus, no job postings, no confirmed headcount and no client-side complaint, so nothing quantifies internal hours lost. Fit (15/20): three of the six capabilities land directly (intake automation, research, CMS integration), and the firm already thinks in agent terms, which shortens the education phase; the deduction is that they sell automation themselves and will push back hard on scope and price. Ability to pay (12/20): 10-50 employees at a ~$50/hr blended rate with a parent group claiming six Inc. fastest-growing appearances and an NJ Fastest 50 listing gives real backing, but the group is a small agency in a contracting sector (NJ professional and business services employment down 0.9% year over year) with only 19+ live projects, so budgets are tight and the buyer will want a fixed-fee pilot. Ease (11/15): small team, two co-founders, one obvious entry point (hello@), no legacy CRM to displace and a public site we can audit before the first call; friction comes from there being no named ops contact, no published address or hours (so no walk-in) and no booking link to shortcut the conversation. Strategic (9/15): agency funnel gaps are a highly repeatable pattern across hundreds of NJ/NY marketing shops and this account would be a credible, AI-literate reference - but a reference whose public claims (5.0/200 reviews vs 100+ projects delivered) need care, and who may in-source what we build. Total 63/100: worth a personalised approach, not a priority tier-1 target.
